mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production index (INDPRO) value (above its 2017 base of 100) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as stronger industrial output supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 100, SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% (indicating an accommodative monetary policy) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as low interest rates reduce the cost of capital and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong housing market activity signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion.
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both increase by > 1% in the past month, SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 7.0%), a declining unemployment rate predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as easing labor market conditions signal improving economic prospects.
failure_condition: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 7.0%), when UNRATE declines, SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 225.0 (indicating elevated inflation) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as high inflation erodes corporate profit margins and prompts monetary tightening.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 225.0, SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A higher employment level (PAYEMS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as stronger labor market conditions support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average, SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) above 600.0 (thousands of units) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong housing market activity signals robust economic growth and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 600.0, SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 225.0) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as the market perceives a 'growth vs. inflation' trade-off that increases equity risk.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 225.0, SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances.
